company.name: Linear
company.oneLiner: Linear sells issue tracking and product planning software for software teams, with built-in agents and automation.
company.customers: Product and engineering teams, from free workspaces to enterprises; the site names OpenAI and Ramp and says it powers over 50,000 product teams.

blueprint.headline: Linear can hand its sales, growth and customer success teams back hours each week and recover lost subscription revenue by drafting the upgrade offers, quotes and renewal plays they now build by hand.

agents.name: Free-to-Paid Upgrade Outreach List
agents.role: Builds a ranked list of Free workspaces nearing the 250-issue or 2-team limit, with a drafted upgrade note to Basic or Business for each, for the growth team.

value.today: Someone exports Free workspaces from the billing and product database into a spreadsheet, eyeballs which ones are near the 250-issue or 2-team cap, and writes upgrade emails one at a time.
value.sizing: Free workspaces near the 250-issue or 2-team limit per month x share that upgrade after outreach x seats per workspace x Basic or Business price per seat x 12

agents.impact: Free teams that are about to hit the 250-issue cap get a well-timed, personal upgrade offer instead of quietly churning or staying on $0.
agents.trigger: Every Monday at 07:00 local, plus on demand from the growth lead.
does: Pull Free workspaces with issue counts, team counts and member counts from the product usage database
Rank workspaces by how close they are to the 250-issue and 2-team limits and by active member count
Draft an upgrade note naming the limit they are approaching and the Basic or Business plan that lifts it
Hand over a ranked sheet with each draft ready to send

humanGate.detail: Every outbound email waits for a growth team member to approve; the agent only saves drafts and never sends.

agents.evidence: The site lists a Free tier with unlimited members, 2 teams and 250 issues, and paid Basic at $10 and Business at $16 per user per month billed yearly.

agents.name: Enterprise Quote and Security Answer Pack
agents.role: Drafts a priced Enterprise or Business proposal and answers the security questionnaire for a sales rep from the buyer's request.

value.today: A rep copies seat counts into a pricing sheet, hunts through past proposals for similar deals, and pastes answers to security questions from old questionnaires and the DPA.
value.sizing: Enterprise and Business deals quoted per month x hours a rep spends on each quote and questionnaire

agents.impact: A rep gets a nearly finished proposal and questionnaire back the same day instead of spending an afternoon assembling it.
agents.trigger: When a rep submits a Contact sales lead record or asks in the sales channel.
does: Read the lead's seat count, segment and requested plan from the CRM
Price the Basic, Business or Enterprise options for that seat count with annual billing
Fill the security questionnaire from approved prior answers and the published DPA, Privacy, Terms and AUP
Assemble a proposal draft with open questions marked for the rep

humanGate.detail: A rep reviews every proposal; any discount, custom term or answer not found in the approved library goes to sales leadership or legal before it is sent.

agents.evidence: The site has a Contact sales option, an Enterprise tier, Enterprise and Startup pages, and published legal policies including Privacy, Terms, DPA and AUP.

agents.name: Renewal Save Plan for Business Accounts
agents.role: Prepares a renewal brief with drafted outreach for each paid account whose seats or activity are dropping, for account managers.

value.today: Account managers compare seat counts and activity in billing and usage exports by hand before renewals and write save emails from scratch.
value.sizing: Accounts renewing per quarter x share showing seat or activity decline x seats lost x per-seat price x 12

agents.impact: Accounts that are shrinking get a tailored save plan before renewal, so seat revenue stops leaking out unnoticed.
agents.trigger: Every Monday at 08:00 local for accounts renewing in the next 60 days.
does: Compare current seats and active users against the prior term for each upcoming renewal
Identify accounts with falling seat counts or inactive teams
Draft a save email and talking points for each account
Hand over a renewal sheet sorted by revenue at risk

humanGate.detail: Account managers approve every message and any discount offer before anything reaches a customer.

agents.evidence: Pricing is per user per month billed yearly on Basic and Business, so seat count at renewal drives revenue.

firstBuild.why: It brings in new subscription revenue from accounts that already use the product, relies on data Linear already holds, and only creates drafts, so risk and integration work are low.
scope: Read Free workspace issue, team and member counts from the usage database
Score workspaces against the 250-issue and 2-team limits
Draft one upgrade note per top workspace for Basic or Business
Deliver a weekly ranked sheet to the growth lead
Add an approval step so nothing is sent without sign-off

blueprint.nonObvious: Linear's Free plan caps issues and teams but not members, so a large team can run on $0 for a long time; the accounts closest to the cap with many active members are the best upgrade targets, not the biggest logos.
caveats: Internal systems such as the CRM, billing and usage database were not visible; categories are assumed.
Enterprise pricing and discount rules were not shown.
Renewal dates and seat history are assumed to be available in billing data.
No sales team size or deal volume was given, so sizing is left as formulas.
